findings.title: Unexpected exceptions skip the cutover report
findings.description:
The module docstring says the first failure stops the run and "the report is still written". `run_steps` only catches `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`. Several steps can raise other exceptions on ordinary host conditions:
- `step_production` and `run_health` call `read_text().splitlines()[-1]`. This raises `IndexError` on an empty log file. `step_production` also raises `FileNotFoundError` if the log is absent, because it has no `exists()` guard.
- `step_weekly` has the same `[-1]` risk on `base.log`.
- `tick_commands()` and `step_check` read `CRON_FILE` unguarded.
- `shell()` and `psql()` have no timeout, so a hung job blocks the run indefinitely.

An uncaught exception skips `report.write_text(...)`. That loses the expected-vs-seen record, which is the main audit trail for a production cutover. Wrap the step call so unexpected exceptions are recorded as FAIL and the report is still written, either with a documented top-level handler or a `try/finally` around the report write. Also guard the empty-file cases explicitly.

findings.title: Production code uses `assert` for runtime narrowing
findings.description: `assert match is not None` and `assert flags is not None` serve as runtime checks. They disappear under `python -O`. In `run_health`, `require(...)` already raises when the condition fails, so the assert only placates the type checker. Return or raise explicitly instead (for example, build the tuple inside the guard).

findings.title: Host facts and argument literals are duplicated instead of sourced from the cluster table
findings.description: `strip_new_args` hardcodes `--replication-host 127.0.0.1`, while the value belongs to the `deploy/backup-clusters.conf` row. `MAIN`/`TICK`, `HOST_BACKUP_ROOT = /data/backup`, `TICK_UNIT` and `RCLONE_REMOTE` are likewise re-declared in the cutover. `deploy/setup-backup.sh` also defines `RCLONE_REMOTE=b2` itself. This breaks the project's "define a value once" rule. If the table changes, the TD3 production-line guard silently diverges, or fails for the wrong reason. Derive the replication host from the production row, and reference the shared constants where possible.

findings.title: Lifecycle read failures are swallowed with `|| true`, but the output parsing covers them
findings.description: `b2_lifecycle.sh`'s exit status is discarded and the code relies on parsing its stdout. This is safe today because every failure path prints a line that maps to `MISSING <cluster> lifecycle-read`, and the unit tests cover it. If the script ever exits non-zero with empty output, the loop would see no lines and report nothing. A one-line guard for an empty `LIFECYCLE_OUT` would make this robust.

findings.title: Cron rendering, cluster table integration and test coverage
findings.description: I confirmed that `deploy/backup-clusters.conf`, `deploy/lib/backup_clusters.sh`, `scripts/backup_clusters.py` and the `cron_main_pre227.txt` fixture exist, and that the `BackupCluster` constructor matches the test fixture. The render logic quotes replacement strings, which protects `2>&1` from bash 5.2+ patsub, and there is a regression test for it. The test against the real pre-227 production file guards the TD3 "only new args added" invariant. The tests cover malformed-table and missing-cluster failures, rehearse root relocation, lifecycle read-only behavior, and a missing lifecycle rule not changing the exit code. The provisioning changes are covered by tests: REPLICATION is opt-in, pg_hba is rendered, and parent directories are 755 while the data directory stays 700. No production-URL reads were introduced in the tests.
